You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "path": "memory/continual-arc-d1ac3b2e.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task-d1ac3b2e notes

## Rule confirmed from 4 demos and a correct test
Input has a background color B and scattered marker color M; output uses new color 3 to draw horizontal and vertical straight segments between markers sharing a row or column. Preserve all original markers and leave other cells unchanged. In each row/column, if there are at least two markers, recolor every strictly-between cell as 3; markers themselves remain M. If fewer than two markers, draw no segment. The output is the union of all such row/column segments; intersections are 3 unless they were marker cells.

Demonstrated across different grids/backgrounds: B=2,M=5 (25x9), B=2,M=1 (25x9), B=1,M=7 (9x30), B=0,M=1 (12x28); on the solved test B=9,M=0 (27x18), applying the row/column-segment rule produced a correct submission. This also explains the apparent strokes as pairwise aligned marker connections, not global fill or convex hull.

Algorithm: copy grid; for each row, find marker columns cmin,cmax; if cmin<cmax, set all non-marker cells in [cmin,cmax] to 3. For each column similarly between min/max marker rows. Preserve all markers. Multiple markers in a line still form the continuous min-to-max stroke.

Caution: a previous attempt to submit an unchanged input was wrong; transform according to strokes. Prior memory from a separate instance claimed an unrelated pattern; prefer the robust rule supported by all demos and this solved grid.
"
